## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under LICENSE.txt.
- [x] Changed-file pre-commit hooks pass and formatting is committed.
- [x] Reviewed applicable AGENTS.md hard rules; support tracker updated (S2).
- [ ] Requested labels: `cat-feature`, `area:frost`, `area:global_attention`, `orig-external` (the external author cannot apply upstream labels).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL (SM120 SDPA forward).

## Summary

Enable FP16/BF16 exact-D128 forward attention with dense queries over paged KV on SM120. Independent K/V block tables and HND/NHD pool layouts bind through the shared prepared validator. The attention CTA copies selected pages directly into the existing swizzled MMA tiles with 16-byte `cp.async`; no gather/repack launch is added.

## Why

The SM120 half engine currently declines paged KV. Reuse its native compute and scheduler while lowering page addressing inside the producer. Dead rows skip table/pool reads and zero-fill shared memory. Each producer lane commits/drains its copies and publishes an async-tracked `.noinc` arrival to the count-32 barrier. Consumers retain their acquire parity waits.

Paged loads already zero-fill the V tail, so the paged leg excludes the legacy redundant compute-warp tail stores that race PV reads. The explicit local copy drain is retained: removing it failed the targeted racecheck. The guide records this ordering contract and the optional-GridConstant descriptor ABI requirement.

## Related issues

Related to #381.

## API and compatibility impact

Scope is dense Q, exact D_QK=D_V=128, FP16/BF16, unsplit M64/M128 prefill. Existing masks, sinks, schedulers and PackGQA compose. K/V pools retain equal page capacities; their tables and layouts are independent. Page size must be divisible by8 and divide128 or be a multiple of128. THD, quantized pools, decode tiles, other heads, split-KV, bias and score side outputs retain declines.

Standalone table operands and template fields are appended with defaults. Unpaged TMA descriptors retain optional `GridConstant` annotations; unpaged compute/publication is unchanged. No graph API, heuristic, workspace format or tolerance change. Execution adds no allocation, host read, layout conversion or runtime JIT. No performance claim; native qualification is cc12.0 only.

## Testing

RTX 6000D (SM120), Python3.12, cuDNN9.27.0.42, Torch2.13+cu130, CuTeDSL4.8.0/CUDA13.4. Private source imports and final kernel hashes verified.

Feature suite reproduction from `test/python`:

```sh
python -m pytest --collect-only -q -k frost sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm120.py
python -m pytest -x -q -s sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm120.py
```

The final source passed all64 collected cases in four disjoint, exhaustive 16-case processes on GPUs4–7: **64 passed, zero skips**, all process/XML statuses zero. All four recorded kernel SHA256 values match `9a5bb4f52c6bfaac00d3c99b47d75a1000da68d5795fc34b07fc593bd45f5b2f`. Coverage includes independent FP64 references, graph/standalone binding, mixed pool layouts, all admitted schedulers, masks, sink/packing combinations, poisoned dead table entries and Q tails, rebinding, retained replay and 520-CTA multiwave reuse. Infinite-sink endpoint transitions return O0 and correct ±inf Stats.

A real physical wide-pool case selects page131073 at an offset above `2**32` elements, poisons the wrapped page, and checks fresh-pool rebinding/replay. It ran without skipping (16GiB pools, 32GiB rebind peak).

```sh
python -m pytest -x -q -s sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_prepared_sm120.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_native_sm120_binding.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_sm120_padding_nan.py
# 234 passed on GPU4; after the final paged-only synchronization edits,
# the original failing dense ABI control and a second dense control also passed (2 passed).
compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --target-processes all --error-exitcode 99 --report-api-errors no python -m pytest sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm120.py -k 'native_rebind_replay or multiwave_replay or single_query or sink_endpoints' -x -q -s
# 14 passed, 50 deselected; ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors; exit0
for tool in racecheck synccheck; do
  compute-sanitizer --tool "$tool" --target-processes all --error-exitcode 99 --report-api-errors no python -m pytest \
    'sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm120.py::test_sm120_frost_paged_native_rebind_replay[2-True-False-8-dtype0]' \
    'sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm120.py::test_sm120_frost_paged_mask_sink_pack_stats[True-True-br_swa-2]' \
    'sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm120.py::test_sm120_frost_paged_sink_endpoints[False--inf]' -x -q -s
done
# 3 passed each, zero hazards/errors; exit0
```

Sanitizer scope is device memory/races/synchronization; independent framework API-probe diagnostics are excluded. The giant physical case runs in the ordinary matrix. Same-host/tool13.2.23 detector controls on GPU4 give valid memory/race exit0 and intentionally bad memory/race exit99 with real diagnostics. No launch dumps are used for pass/fail.

CUDA profiling records exactly one attributable cuDNN kernel for each FP16/BF16 graph execute. Baseline RED, exact SASS mapping of the tail-store race, isolated fix controls, and final qualification are retained. Independent spec/code review cleared the final protocol. Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

## API-tail contract integration follow-up

Updated the same stale contract for SM120 page-table operands in 8a18bc7: sf_o retains its position, followed by block_table=None and block_table_v=None. Existing sf_o checks and other architecture expectations remain. Entire API contract module: 14 passed; native paged/frame controls: 34 passed. No production or kernel changes. Fresh FROST CI requested for 8a18bc7.

+A paged producer that zero-fills invalid rows must not also run legacy
+compute-warp tail sanitation. Multiple compute warps can then overwrite V
+while another warp reads it through `ldmatrix`, even when the stores repeat
+zero. The SM120 paged racecheck maps these accesses to `STS.128` tail stores
+and PV `LDSM` reads. Keep the TMA-only sanitizer on unpaged paths that need it.
+For per-thread `cp.async` production, use an async-tracked mbarrier arrival
+(`cp_async_mbarrier_arrive(noinc=True)` with all lane arrivals counted at init),
+rather than publishing those copies with an ordinary mbarrier arrival. The
+qualified SM120 loader also retains producer-local commit/wait-group completion:
+an async-arrival-only variant passed numerics but failed the same racecheck.
+Do not remove that drain without rerunning the native sanitizer/capture cases.
+See the [PTX mbarrier completion rules](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/)
+and run the native paging racecheck as well as memcheck and numerical replay.

+**Native D128 paged forward.** Exact FP16/BF16 D128 dense queries may read
+independent K/V block tables and HND/NHD page pools through the common prepared
+graph and standalone contracts. The attention CTA copies each selected page
+segment directly into its existing swizzled MMA shared tile, zero-filling rows
+past the device KV length; there is no materialized gather/repack or additional
+launch. K/V pools retain equal physical page capacities. Query and KV lengths,
+per-operand strides, pointers and table contents bind at execution and replay.
+This leg uses TILE_M 64/128 with TILE_N 64/128 and split_kv=1; other head
+shapes, THD Q, quantization and the decode tiles remain declined. Existing mask,
+sink, packing and Stats semantics compose without a heuristic change. Paged
+sink endpoints retain O=0 / Stats=+inf for a +inf sink, and O=0 / Stats=-inf
+for a keyless row with a -inf sink.
+`test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm120.py` pins the native SM120 route and checks FP64 O/Stats,
+poisoned dead pages/tails, mixed pool layouts including singleton heads,
+rebinding, capture/replay, sink endpoints, physical page-offset products above
+2**32 elements, and storage canaries. The physical wide-pool case requires
+40 GiB free and runs outside sanitizer; compact cases retain sanitizer coverage.
+
 Base-2 stats are wired into all four f16 templates (the decode tile included) and
 the FP8 and MXFP8 templates, including the final Split-KV combine. `sdpa_mxfp8` graphs take no
 `stats_use_log2` input, so only the direct adapter reaches the MXFP8 wiring.

+def _check(bufs, page, *, mask="none", stats_log2=False):
+    q = bufs["q"].double()
+    h, kh = q.shape[1], bufs["k"].shape[1]
+    for batch, length in enumerate(bufs["kl"].flatten().tolist()):
+        qlength = int(bufs["ql"].flatten()[batch])
+        pools = []
+        for name, table in [("k", "kt"), ("v", "vt")]:
+            rows = [bufs[name][int(bufs[table][batch, 0, i // page, 0]), :, i % page] for i in range(length)]
+            tensor = torch.stack(rows, dim=1).double() if rows else q.new_empty((kh, 0, 128))
+            pools.append(tensor.repeat_interleave(h // kh, dim=0))
+        scores = q[batch] @ pools[0].transpose(-1, -2) / math.sqrt(128)
+        qr = torch.arange(q.shape[2], device=q.device)[:, None]
+        kr = torch.arange(length, device=q.device)[None, :]
+        visible = qr < qlength
+        if mask != "none":
+            diagonal = qr + (length - qlength if mask == "br_swa" else 0)
+            visible = visible & (kr <= diagonal + (3 if mask == "band" else 0))
+            if mask == "br_swa":
+                visible = visible & (kr >= diagonal - 19)
+        scores.masked_fill_(~visible, -float("inf"))
+        values = pools[1]
+        if "sink" in bufs:
+            sink = bufs["sink"].flatten().double()[:, None, None].expand(h, q.shape[2], 1).clone()
+            sink.masked_fill_((qr >= qlength)[None], -float("inf"))
+            scores = torch.cat((scores, sink), dim=-1)
+            values = torch.cat((values, values.new_zeros(h, 1, 128)), dim=1)
+        ref = torch.nan_to_num(scores.softmax(-1), nan=0.0) @ values
+        torch.testing.assert_close(bufs["o"][batch].double(), ref, atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-2)
+        lse = scores.logsumexp(-1) * (math.log2(math.e) if stats_log2 else 1.0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(bufs["stats"][batch].double(), lse, atol=3e-4, rtol=3e-4)
